articles.title: There is only one Global South phrase for the APEC agenda: debt relief
articles.author: Vijay Prashad
articles.content_excerpt: In October, I visited a steel factory in Xinyu, Jiangxi province. There was no dust in the factory. At a desk, a woman wearing an orange hard hat monitored the production of silicon-steel strips. Her attention moved between the machinery and her keyboard. “Keep the belt at the proper speed,” she said. The precision of the process depended on her knowledge as much as on the equipment before her. Here was innovation at work, sustained by the skills of a worker. That scene stayed with me as I considered the forthcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen. A factory requires more than a machine purchased on the world market, it requires reliable electricity, transportation, technical education, and the accumulated capabilities of an industrial workforce. articles.title: ASEAN summit in Manila met with protests over Trump’s participation
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: The 49th summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) opened in Manila, the Philippines on Sunday, November 15, amid large-scale protests against the presence of US President Donald Trump. Security forces clashed with protesters, injuring several and detaining hundreds, as they tried to march towards the Philippines International Convention Center. The protesters, carrying posters and banners with slogans against the US and Trump, the illegal war against Iran, and the proposed Pax Silica project in the country, tried to march to the venue of the summit despite police calling the protests illegal and erecting barricades to stop them. articles.title: The fall of the ANC
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: Securing less than 31% of the votes in the local election held earlier this month, the African National Congress (ANC) has delivered its weakest ever electoral performance in over three decades of South Africa’s post-apartheid era. Held amid worsening water shortages, power disruptions, and piling uncollected garbage, the party saw its vote share drop by almost 15 percentage points from the 45.6% it received in the 2021 local elections. The number of council seats it secured dropped over 30%, from 4,548 in 2021 to 3,164 in 2026.​ Even steeper is the more than 68% decline in the number of municipalities where it has an outright majority. articles.content_excerpt: The United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, is in its second and final week.
